author: taratorio
content: why does the shadow fork have `7,896 MGas` blocks? cc <@577788234810130432>

author: taratorio
content: it is not an issue that can happen on mainnet with 200Mgas blocks, however it highlighted something that we should not be doing - we still had code from the very first iteration of the BAL implementation which was doing DOS protection based on RLP size, not based on the current block gas limit based rule. will remove that code and we should be compliant

author: parithosh
content:
Not sure, he set it up while we’re were asleep and said explicitly “don’t look at the gas limit”😅 
So I’m guessing there’s a reason and we’d need to wait for him to wake up for it

author: taratorio
content: all good, it actually highlighted some old code leftovers that we have forgotten to remove. ill tidy this up shortly

author: qu0b
content: Sorry quite a few things did not go as planned for this network

author: taratorio
content: hmm but wait actually probably we should have some RLP size limit. otherwise you might get a very large RLP that you need to decode before you get to the `bal_items <= block_gas_limit // ITEM_COST` check in the current spec. i think this relates to  what was raised in https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1364000387195076608/1547191157476433940. so maybe we should add such a rlp size limit to the spec to avoid such client discrepancies  <@792404665068158998> ? for example i checked how long it takes to decode a BAL RLP close to 10MiB (the devp2p limit) filled with majority storage reads and it took around 385-500ms

author: taratorio
content: actually this is probably not worth the discussion. it can be optimised down to ~20-ish ms so not a big deal without the rlp size limit

author: nero_eth
content:
yeah I tried some decoding bombs too after <@806184091690598420> brought it up in the bal channel and couldn't find any issues as well.
The size limit we have is the 10 mib payload size limit.

author: nero_eth
content: but yeah, there are simple heuristics - not spec'ed - allowing clients to optimize rejecting invalid blocks early

author: taratorio
content:
ok, ill just update erigon's limit to 10mib and we're fine
this was more of an issue with extremely high gas usage on the shadow fork tbh

author: nero_eth
content: the CLs should enforce the limit already, so, you'd be protecting against a malicious/faulty CL

author: nero_eth
content: actually, might still make sense for sync, bal exchange etc.

author: taratorio
content:
we already have the 10mib protection at the devp2p layer (larger messages get dropped)
the only uncovered case is untrusted relays as <@806184091690598420> mentioned since those might circumvent the CL enforced limit?

author: taratorio
content: it's easy to add the 10mib early rejection when decoding to cover that case too but it might be better if it is mentioned in the EIP for clarity
